title_en: Junxin Venture Company v. Lvgu Weiye Company et al. — dispute over capital contribution contract
ruling_gist_en: When both parties present contrary evidence on the same fact but neither party has sufficient grounds to disprove the other party's evidence, the party bearing the burden of proof for that fact shall bear the consequences of failing to meet the burden of proof.
keywords_en: Civil; Capital contribution contract dispute; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region; Shanghai; Legal person; Civil Procedure Law; Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings; Determination of false capital contribution; Allocation of burden of proof; Evidentiary effect; Affirmation of original judgment; Capital increase and share expansion; Equity transfer; Contract dispute; Capital contribution dispute (Guweiye Company et al.)
full_text_en:
Junxin Venture Capital Co., Ltd. v. Lvgu Weiye Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Capital Contribution Contract

【Ruling Summary】

Where the parties to a case have adduced contrary evidence on the same facts but none of the evidence is sufficient to rebut the other party's evidence, the party bearing the burden of proof for the facts of the case shall assume the consequences of failure to discharge that burden.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 260

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Ningxia Junxin Venture Capital Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 101, No. 7, Science and Technology Street, Development Zone, Yinchuan City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Hou Yuqian, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Wang Lei, Lawyer of Jintianping Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Shanghai Lvgu Weiye Ecological Engineering Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 2615, No. 1688, North Sichuan Road, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Wu Tongxin, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Wang Junling, Lawyer of Jingcheng Law Firm, Shanghai.

Third Party at First Instance: Ningxia Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Domicile: West of Road 15, South of Road 4, High-tech Development Zone, Yinchuan City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Wang Zhongxiao, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Ding Liang, Lawyer of Guangming Law Firm, Shanghai.

The Appellant, Ningxia Junxin Venture Capital Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Junxin Company), being dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2003) Ning Min Shang Chu Zi No. 17 rendered by the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region in the case concerning a dispute over capital contribution contract with the Respondent, Shanghai Lvgu Weiye Ecological Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lvgu Weiye Company), and the Third Party at First Instance, Ningxia Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.), appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law, composed of Presiding Judge Wu Qingbao, Acting Judges Gong Bangyou and Liu Min, to hear the case, with Clerk Zhao Suijun keeping the record. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial the following facts: In June 1998, Ningxia Oriental Shencao Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. was established by joint investment of the Ningxia Institute of Materia Medica (hereinafter referred to as the Institute) and Shanghai Lvgu Group, with a registered capital of RMB 10,000,000, of which the Institute contributed RMB 7,000,000 (by way of investment in kind); Shanghai Lvgu Group contributed RMB 3,000,000 (RMB 1,600,000 in cash and RMB 1,400,000 in raw materials in kind). In August of the same year, Ningxia Oriental Shencao Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. was renamed Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. In March 2000, Shanghai Lvgu Group transferred all of its shares and all rights and interests in Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. to Lvgu Weiye Company. On August 1, 2000, the shareholders' meeting of Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. resolved to increase capital and issue new shares, increasing the registered capital of Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. to RMB 38,000,000. It was decided that the Institute would increase its capital contribution by RMB 12,000,000, and Lvgu Weiye Company would increase its capital contribution by RMB 16,000,000; after the increase, the Institute and Lvgu Weiye Company would each hold 50% of the shares of Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.; the new capital contributions should be paid in full in installments before September 30, 2000. On September 6, 2000, the shareholders' meeting of Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. resolved to approve the Institute's transfer of all its 19,000,000 shares in Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., of which 2,000,000 shares were transferred to the Plaintiff, Junxin Company, and 1,000,000 shares to Inner Mongolia Linhe Xingke Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. It approved Lvgu Weiye Company's transfer of part of its shares, of which 3,000,000 shares were transferred to Beijing Dadi Science and Technology Industry Corporation, 1,000,000 shares to Beijing Junyi Runtai Investment Consulting Co., Ltd., and 2,000,000 shares to Shanghai Beirong Asset Management Co., Ltd. All original shareholders unanimously agreed to waive their preemptive rights in this share transfer. In October 2000, the aforementioned parties entered into the "Sponsors' Agreement," stipulating: 1. to convert Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. into Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.; 2. each sponsor shall fulfill its capital contribution obligation within 10 days after the approval of the company's conversion; 3. the registered capital of the company is RMB 38,000,000; 4. if a sponsor fails to make its capital contribution within the time limit and in the amount specified in this agreement, for each day of default, the defaulting party shall pay a penalty of five thousandths of the defaulted capital contribution amount to the performing party, and such penalty shall be distributed among the performing parties in proportion to their capital contributions. There were fifteen records of Lvgu Weiye Company's increased capital contribution of RMB 16,000,000. The investments were made from September 24, 1999, to September 18, 2000. Among them, RMB 7,870,000 was remitted on behalf of Lvgu Weiye Company by Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. The remainder was remitted from accounts related to Lvgu Weiye Company. The total amount was RMB 16,000,000. Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. issued corresponding capital contribution receipts to Lvgu Weiye Company. Subsequently, the Institute and Lvgu Weiye Company actually completed the share transfers. Both Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and the current Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. acknowledged that Lvgu Weiye Company's investment of RMB 16,000,000 had actually been made in full. Verified by a capital verification institution, the capital contributions of all shareholders were in place, and a capital verification report was issued, which was registered with the industrial and commercial authorities.

It was further found: In February 1997, Shanghai Lvgu Group and the Institute jointly invested to establish Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., now renamed Ningxia Boertaili Pharmaceutical Marketing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Marketing Company). Shanghai Lvgu Group contributed RMB 4,000,000 in kind and RMB 500,000 in cash; the Institute contributed RMB 500,000 in kind, with a registered capital of RMB 5,000,000. In December 1998, Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. increased its capital and expanded its shares, increasing the registered capital to RMB 10,000,000, of which Shanghai Lvgu Group held RMB 7,000,000 and the Institute held RMB 3,000,000, with Shanghai Lvgu Group holding control. In March 2000, Shanghai Lvgu Group transferred all its shares in Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. to Lvgu Weiye Company. In September 2000, after Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (the parent company) completed its capital increase and share expansion, Shanghai Lvgu Weiye Company and the Institute transferred 90% of the shares of Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (the subsidiary) to Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Lvgu Weiye Company and the Institute each retained 5% of the shares. On October 21, 2003, Junxin Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, claiming that Lvgu Weiye Company had failed to make its capital contribution in full, and requested a judgment ordering Lvgu Weiye Company to bear liability for breach of contract towards Junxin Company, in order to protect its lawful rights and interests from infringement.

The High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region held that the disputed issue in this case was whether Lvgu Weiye Company had made a false capital contribution.

The main evidence submitted by Junxin Company, the "Audit Investigation Report of the Ningxia Audit Office on Issues Concerning Equity Investment of Ningxia Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.," was an internal audit investigation report submitted to the leaders of the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region Government by the Ningxia Audit Office after it conducted an audit investigation into the state-owned assets of Ningxia Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., and did not meet the formal requirements for civil litigation evidence and the evidentiary requirements for expert conclusions, and therefore was not admitted. Other evidence from Junxin Company could only prove the specific form and source of funds for Lvgu Weiye Company's capital contribution. Neither Junxin Company nor Lvgu Weiye Company applied for an audit appraisal during the trial at first instance. The court held that whether Lvgu Weiye Company had made a false capital contribution involved specialized issues of corporate financial management. According to the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," based on the evidence provided by Junxin Company at first instance, it could not be determined whether Lvgu Weiye Company had made a false capital contribution. Therefore, Junxin Company's claims could not be sustained. Pursuant to Article 128 of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" and Paragraph 2 of Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," the court rendered the following judgment: 1. Junxin Company's claims were dismissed; 2. Court acceptance fee of RMB 87,360 and preservation fee of RMB 77,870, totaling RMB 165,230, were borne by Junxin Company.

Junxin Company, being dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, appealed to this Court, stating: First, the original judgment did not evaluate the views and reasons of the appellant and the respondent on the focal issue of whether the respondent, Lvgu Weiye Company, had made a false capital contribution. Instead, it relied on the "capital contribution receipts" issued by the third party (formerly Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.), which was controlled by the respondent, and the "capital verification report" issued by an intermediary institution commissioned in the name of the controlled company to determine that the respondent had made its capital contribution in full. However, such documents could be forged or issued in accordance with the will of the respondent, especially against the background that the respondent had always controlled the third party and Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and had always held a dominant position in the historical evolution of these two companies. By checking the financial accounts of the Marketing Company, the appellant discovered that neither the former Shanghai Lvgu Group nor the current respondent had made the investment amounts claimed in the audit reports and capital verification reports of the intermediary institutions. The "Reconciliation Statement" provided by the respondent was prepared during the period when it controlled Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., and the audit reports and capital verification reports of the intermediary institutions were also commissioned and issued during the period when it controlled Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. The authenticity and objectivity of such documents are difficult to accept. Second, regarding the issue of how to determine the evidentiary validity of the "Audit Investigation Report of the Ningxia Audit Office on Issues Concerning Equity Investment of Ningxia Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.," the original judgment confused documentary evidence with expert conclusions. When providing this evidence, the appellant did not use it solely as an expert conclusion but as documentary evidence because its content was consistent with the facts found by the appellant itself. The audit investigation report of the Ningxia Audit Office was an internal document prepared after the Audit Office discovered the respondent's false capital contribution during an audit of state-owned assets. The audit office had no connection with the parties in this case. Moreover, the court of first instance specifically verified and cross-examined this report, so its evidentiary validity should be affirmed. According to the standard of proof of "preponderance of the evidence," the public documentary evidence produced by a state authority in the exercise of its functions, as provided by the appellant, has stronger probative force than the evidence produced unilaterally by the respondent and the evidence unilaterally commissioned from a social intermediary institution. Even without the audit investigation report of the Ningxia Audit Office, based on the appellant's request to obtain evidence, the respondent should have provided its financial accounts but refused to do so, indicating that those accounts were unfavorable to it. Therefore, the court should, in accordance with the inference rules, presume that the appellant's claims are valid. The original judgment held that "whether the defendant made a false capital contribution involves specialized issues of corporate financial management" and "the plaintiff's existing evidence cannot determine whether the defendant made a false capital contribution." If so, the court of first instance should have, ex officio, entrusted an intermediary institution to conduct an audit on this issue. However, it failed to do so, resulting in a failure to clarify a question that could have been clarified and refusing to draw conclusions that could have been drawn. This not only violated the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings" but also the adjudicative principle that "a court cannot refuse to render a judgment." In summary, the appellant, Junxin Company, believes that the original judgment erred both in fact and in the application of law, and requests that the court of second instance set aside the original judgment; order the respondent to make up the capital contribution of RMB 13,070,000 or, if it cannot do so, reduce the respondent's corresponding shares in the third party; and order the respondent to pay the appellant RMB 3,090,000 in liquidated damages for false capital contribution constituting a breach of contract.

The respondent, Lvgu Weiye Company, argued in its defense: The audit investigation report issued by the Ningxia Audit Office provided by the appellant does not meet the requirements of "authenticity," "relevance," and "lawfulness" for the use of evidence in litigation as set forth in the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings." 1. The source of the evidence is unclear: The audit report submitted by the appellant to the court of first instance was only a copy, without the seal of the auditing institution and without the signatures of the specific auditors. During the trial at first instance, the appellant could not explain the lawful source of the audit report, claiming only that it was provided by its parent company, Ningxia Saint Snow Rong International Group Co., Ltd. 2. The process of forming the evidence was unlawful: The "Audit Law of the People's Republic of China" clearly stipulates that the auditing targets of an audit authority are state-owned enterprises, enterprises in which state-owned assets hold a controlling or dominant position; the audit authority shall deliver an audit notice to the audited entity three days before the audit; and the audit report shall seek the opinions of the audited entity before being delivered to the audit authority. Among the total 38,000,000 shares of the seven sponsors that established the third party, Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., there was not a single state-owned enterprise or enterprise in which state-owned assets held a controlling or dominant position. Furthermore, the Audit Office did not seek the opinions of the third party or its subsidiaries during the audit process, nor did it seek the opinions of the company's shareholders or board of directors. Therefore, this audit was neither a statutory audit nor a joint audit commissioned by the parties; it neither provided the legal basis for the audit nor the evidentiary materials used during the audit process, nor did it provide the legal and factual basis for the conclusions. 3. The audit report is an isolated piece of evidence: Based on all the evidence submitted by Junxin Company at first instance, the audit investigation report of the Ningxia Audit Office was the only evidence used by Junxin Company to support its claims and to deny the authenticity of the evidence provided by Lvgu Weiye Company. The conclusions of this audit report contradict the contents and conclusions of previous audit reports issued by accounting firms jointly commissioned by all shareholders of the third party, but the appellant failed to adduce evidence related to or corroborating the facts and conclusions recorded in the audit report. (b) The probative force of the audit report submitted by the appellant is not stronger than that of the evidence submitted by the respondent, and the "preponderance of the evidence" standard cannot be used to deny the evidence submitted by the respondent. First, according to the facts found at first instance, the respondent's capital increase to the third party occurred first, while the third party's borrowing from Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. occurred later. The respondent never became the controlling shareholder of the third party, nor did it engage in conduct of fabricating false debts by taking advantage of its controlling position. Moreover, during the same period, when the third party acquired the shares of Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. held by the respondent, it should have paid the respondent RMB 7,670,000 as consideration for the share transfer. This amount was not paid by the third party to the respondent until April 2003. At that time, the respondent could have converted its creditor's right against the third party into equity in the third party, thereby achieving the purpose of capital increase. Therefore, the respondent argues that the appellant's conclusion is merely an inference without legal basis. Second, the appellant uses only the audit investigation report to prove its inference, thereby evading its burden of proof. Furthermore, the respondent argues that the previous capital verification reports and audit reports it submitted to the collegiate panel during the trial at first instance were commissioned jointly by all shareholders of the third party and were issued by intermediary institutions that had no connection with the shareholders, the respondent, or the third party. These reports were recognized by all shareholders and accepted by the relevant administrative authorities for filing. The respondent contends that the probative force of this series of evidence is greater than that of the single audit investigation report submitted by the appellant.

The third party, Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., did not participate in the appeal proceedings and made no submissions.

In addition to the facts found by the court of first instance, during the appeal, the appellant, Junxin Company, submitted to this Court the Administrative Judgment (2004) Yin Xing Zhong Zi No. 63 of the Intermediate People's Court of Yinchuan City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, and the Administrative Judgment (2004) Xing Xing Chu Zi No. 52 of the Xingqing District People's Court of Yinchuan City.

This Court finds through trial: The fact to be proved in this case is whether, during the capital increase and share expansion of Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (later renamed Ningxia Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.), the respondent, Lvgu Weiye Company, engaged in false capital contribution by means of using its controlling position to fabricate debts and carry out circular funds. The focus of the dispute is the determination of the probative force of the evidence of both parties.

1. The main evidence of the appellant, Junxin Company — the "Audit Investigation Report of the Ningxia Audit Office on Issues Concerning Equity Investment of Ningxia Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd." — was verified and cross-examined by the court of first instance. It was an internal audit investigation report submitted to the leaders of the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region Government by the Ningxia Audit Office after it conducted an audit investigation into the state-owned assets of Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., and it concerned the capital contribution situation of the respondent, Lvgu Weiye Company. Its evidentiary nature is that of documentary evidence, not an expert conclusion issued by an auditing department commissioned by a judicial organ. Moreover, this audit report also failed to directly and sufficiently prove the fact of the respondent's false capital contribution, and it cannot be used as the basis for deciding the case: (1) The audit conducted by the Ningxia Audit Office was not a statutory audit. According to the relevant provisions of the "Audit Law of the People's Republic of China" and the "Implementing Regulations of the Audit Law of the People's Republic of China," the auditing targets of an audit authority are the fiscal revenues and expenditures of the departments of the State Council and local people's governments at all levels and their departments, the financial revenues and expenditures of state-owned financial institutions and enterprises and institutions, and the fiscal revenues and expenditures of other state-owned enterprises and enterprises in which state-owned assets hold a controlling or dominant position that should be subject to audit in accordance with the provisions of the Audit Law. Among the total 38,000,000 shares of the seven sponsors that established the third party, Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., there was not a single state-owned enterprise or enterprise in which state-owned assets held a controlling or dominant position. Therefore, this was not within the audit scope of the Audit Office. (2) This audit was not a joint audit commissioned by the parties to the dispute. It was an internal audit investigation report submitted to the leaders of the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region Government by the Ningxia Audit Office after it conducted an audit investigation into the state-owned assets of Boertaili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., and it concerned the capital contribution situation of the respondent, Lvgu Weiye Company. It is hearsay evidence and circumstantial evidence, lacking specificity. (3) The audit report did not provide the legal basis for the audit nor the evidentiary materials used during the audit process, nor did it provide the legal and factual basis for the conclusions. Therefore, it is not recognized. Regarding the validity of the two administrative judgments provided by the appellant during the appeal, although the probative force of this audit report was recognized in those two administrative judgments, they are not materially connected to this case and cannot therefore enhance the probative force of this evidence.

Second, the Appellee provided evidence including a reconciliation statement with Ningxia Lvgu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., a relevant capital verification report filed with the company registration authority, capital contribution certificates and receipts from the Appellee to the third party, and an audit report issued by an intermediary commissioned jointly by the shareholders of the third party, to prove that it had fully and truthfully performed its capital increase obligations. The Appellant did not recognize the probative value of the evidence provided by the Appellee, arguing that such documents were unilaterally produced by the Appellee or by companies it controlled, or were issued by unilaterally commissioned intermediaries, and could all be forged or issued in accordance with the Appellee's will, and requested the Appellee to provide its original financial accounts. With respect to the Appellee's refusal to provide its original accounts, the Appellant asserted the application of the presumption rule, arguing that the Appellee should have provided its financial accounts but refused to do so, indicating that such accounts were unfavorable to the Appellee, and therefore it should be presumed that the Appellant's claim was established. In this regard, this Court holds that the Appellant's denial of the probative value of the Appellee's series of evidence and the Appellee's refusal to provide its original financial accounts have, to a certain extent, weakened the probative value of the evidence provided by the Appellee, but do not necessarily lead to the conclusion that the Appellee made false capital contributions.

In conclusion, this Court holds that although the two parties have each presented contrary evidence on the same facts, neither has sufficient basis to refute the other's evidence. Due to the limited probative value of the evidence, no finding favorable to the Appellant can be made. Moreover, Junxin Company did not apply for a commissioned audit to determine whether Lvgu Weiye Company had made defective capital contributions in either the first or second instance, nor did it further produce evidence favorable to itself. Therefore, its grounds of appeal and claims cannot be sustained, and this Court dismisses them. The facts found by the court of first instance are substantially consistent with those found by this Court, and the law was correctly applied. The judgment of first instance shall be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 73 and Article 2 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the Appellant, Junxin Company, which bears the burden of proof for the facts of this case, shall bear the consequences of failing to produce sufficient evidence. In accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 2 and 73 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the judgment is as follows:

Appeal dismissed; original judgment affirmed.

First and second instance case acceptance fees of RMB 87,360 each, and first instance preservation fee of RMB 77,870, are all to be borne by the Appellant, Ningxia Junxin Venture Capital Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wu Qingbao

Acting Judge: Gong Bangyou

Acting Judge: Liu Min

March 7, 2005

Clerk: Zhao Suijun
